abstract: The eukaryotic pathogen, vector, and host informatics resource (VEuPathDB, https://veupathdb.org) provides open access to genomic and other large-scale data for protozoan and fungal pathogens, arthropod vectors, and their hosts, supporting >800 organisms and 2602 datasets across 12 component databases, OrthoMCL, and the newly added dataExplorer, as of Release 71 (August 2026). Since our last update, 292 datasets have been integrated, gene product descriptions improved, and OrthoMCL expanded to over 819 000 orthology groups spanning 9.2 million proteins. Artificial intelligence-assisted approaches now support dataset curation, community gene annotation, and experimental summaries of transcriptomic evidence on gene pages, each subject to expert or user review. The new My Datasets workspace lets researchers upload, analyze, and share their own data alongside curated datasets, and a guided interface supports differential expression analysis without programming. Infrastructure has been consolidated from 15 Oracle databases into a single PostgreSQL platform, with data-processing pipelines migrated to containerized Nextflow workflows. This period was also defined by the loss of the long-standing US federal award that funded VEuPathDB, its temporary closure in September 2024, and its restoration under a community-supported model of voluntary tiered subscriptions, donations, and philanthropic support, with all data and tools remaining freely accessible.
